title: Cluster-aware SVD upcycling with shared View basis
hypothesis: A shared cross-cluster residual basis plus cluster/member codes preserves cluster-aware expert behavior at lower complete bytes than separate cluster-specific SVD subspaces and full experts.
physical_object: cluster-specific expert subspaces discovered from semantic groups
mirror_coordinate: shared basis coordinates indexed by semantic cluster and expert role
logical_multiplicity: twelve upcycled experts across three semantic clusters

development.selection_metric: heldout routed operator nRMSE, router accuracy, actual bytes and reconstruction MAC

fresh.reason: native shared-basis control is evaluated before fresh access

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Shared View basis preserves heldout routing and operator quality with >=25% fewer complete bytes than full experts and a strict gain over native global PCA and cluster-specific SVD at matched compute.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if native PCA matches the shared codes or byte/quality/compute gates fail.
boundaries: Synthetic linear experts with known semantic clusters; no trained Cluster-Aware Upcycling or self-distillation claim.
Routing is nearest-centroid classification on synthetic activations; router state is fully serialized.
Cluster-specific SVD and global PCA are direct native controls.
